contentObjective: I can construct an argument using equations, drawings, or words, and use volume to defend a recommendation.
languageObjective: I can explain my thinking with clear math vocabulary using the words argument, conjecture, and cubic units.

vocabulary.definition: A chain of reasons — equations, drawings, or words — used to defend your thinking.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una cadena de razones — ecuaciones, dibujos o palabras — que usas para defender tu pensamiento.
vocabulary.example: I recommend two jumbo boxes because their total volume is greater.
vocabulary.cloze: A chain of reasons used to defend your thinking is an ___.

examples.text: A claim followed by the computation that supports it
examples.why: The reasons are attached to the claim.
A claim with no reasons behind it convinces nobody.

vocabulary.definition: A mathematical statement you believe is true but have not yet proven.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una afirmación matemática que crees verdadera pero que aún no has probado.
vocabulary.example: I think the two jumbo boxes hold more cereal than the three large boxes.
vocabulary.visual: “A bigger box ALWAYS holds more cereal” — believed, not yet proven.
vocabulary.cloze: A statement you believe is true but have not yet proven is a ___.

examples.text: “I think the two jumbo boxes hold more cereal.”
examples.why: It is a checkable claim that still needs an argument.
That is a definition already established, not a claim to test.

vocabulary.definition: A single example that shows a statement is not always true.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un solo ejemplo que muestra que una afirmación no siempre es verdadera.
vocabulary.example: One box with more volume but more empty air space inside.
vocabulary.visual: One jumbo box sold half full of air breaks “bigger always holds more”.
vocabulary.cloze: A single case that shows a statement is not always true is a ___.

examples.text: A larger box holding less cereal than a smaller one
examples.why: One case is enough to make the ALWAYS claim false.

examples.text: Another box that fits the claim
examples.why: Agreeing examples never disprove a statement.

vocabulary.definition: The amount of space a solid figure takes up, measured in cubic units.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad de espacio que ocupa una figura sólida, medida en unidades cúbicas.
vocabulary.example: A garden bed 4 ft long, 3 ft wide, and 2 ft deep has a volume of 24 cubic feet.
vocabulary.visual: 8 in × 3 in × 10 in = 240 cubic inches of cereal space.
vocabulary.cloze: The amount of space a solid figure takes up, in cubic units, is its ___.

examples.text: How much soil fills a 4 ft × 2 ft × 1 ft planter
examples.why: It measures the space inside, in cubic units.

examples.text: How much wrapping paper covers the box
examples.why: That is surface area — the outside, not the inside.

vocabulary.definition: A cube with edges 1 unit long — the unit used to measure volume.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un cubo cuyas aristas miden 1 unidad — la unidad que se usa para medir el volumen.
vocabulary.example: The community garden needs 48 cubic feet of soil.
vocabulary.visual: One cube, 1 unit on every edge — the block volume is counted in.
vocabulary.cloze: A cube with edges 1 unit long, used to measure volume, is a ___ ___.

examples.why: A cube 1 foot on each edge.
A square unit covers flat space; it has no depth.

2. Use accurate units and vocabulary (e.g. cubic units for volume)
3. Test with counterexamples to verify that the rule holds true every time

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Another Option for the Community Garden
revealWordProblem.text:
Another design for the community garden bed, shown here, is also being considered. Both designs are built from rectangular boxes with the same depth.
Question: Which garden bed design would you recommend, and why?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Two labeled garden-bed designs built from rectangular boxes, with side lengths marked in feet.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: I broke each design into rectangular boxes, used the labeled lengths to find the area (or volume) of each box, and added the parts to get a total for each design. Then I compared the totals and recommended the design with more planting space for the same depth. I named the numbers I compared so my recommendation is backed by the measurements, not just by how the design looks.

questions.stem: An egg muffin is about 60 calories. A plate holds 4 egg muffins. About how many calories are on the plate?
questions.explanation: 4 muffins at about 60 calories each is 60 × 4 = 240 calories.
choiceFeedback: That divides 60 by 4 instead of multiplying.
That multiplies 60 by 10 instead of by 4.
hints: How many muffins, and how many calories in each one?
4 equal groups of 60.
Multiply 60 × 4.
questions.stemEs: Un panecillo de huevo tiene unas 60 calorías. Un plato lleva 4 panecillos de huevo. ¿Aproximadamente cuántas calorías hay en el plato?
questions.explanationEs: 4 panecillos de unas 60 calorías cada uno es 60 × 4 = 240 calorías.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántos panecillos, y cuántas calorías tiene cada uno?
4 grupos iguales de 60.
Multiplica 60 × 4.

questions.stem: A large cereal box is 8 in long, 3 in wide, and 10 in tall. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume of a rectangular prism is length × width × height: 8 × 3 × 10 = 240 cubic inches.
choiceFeedback: That adds 8 + 3 + 10 instead of multiplying the dimensions.
That multiplies only 8 × 10 and leaves out the 3-inch width.
The number is right, but volume is measured in CUBIC inches — square inches measure area.
hints: Volume of a box is length × width × height.
Multiply 8 × 3 first, then use the height.
questions.stemEs: Una caja grande de cereal mide 8 pulgadas de largo, 3 de ancho y 10 de alto. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
questions.explanationEs: El volumen de un prisma rectangular es largo × ancho × alto: 8 × 3 × 10 = 240 pulgadas cúbicas.
hintsEs: El volumen de una caja es largo × ancho × alto.
Multiplica primero 8 × 3 y luego usa la altura.

questions.stem: Each jumbo box holds 400 cubic inches. How much do TWO jumbo boxes hold?
questions.explanation: Two boxes of 400 cubic inches each is 400 × 2 = 800 cubic inches.
choiceFeedback: That divides 400 by 2 instead of doubling.
That multiplies 400 by 10 instead of by 2.
hints: Two equal boxes — what operation combines them?
Double 400.
questions.stemEs: Cada caja jumbo contiene 400 pulgadas cúbicas. ¿Cuánto contienen DOS cajas jumbo?
questions.explanationEs: Dos cajas de 400 pulgadas cúbicas cada una son 400 × 2 = 800 pulgadas cúbicas.
hintsEs: Dos cajas iguales — ¿qué operación las combina?
Duplica 400.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: Reporting volume without cubic units — saying the garden needs '48 feet' of soil, which is a length, or '48 square feet', which is an area.

level1.stem: A box is 2 inches long, 5 inches wide, and 7 inches tall. What is its volume?
level1.stemEs: Una caja mide 2 pulgadas de largo, 5 de ancho y 7 de alto. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
hints: Multiply length × width × height.
hintsEs: Multiplica largo × ancho × alto.
level1.explanation: Multiply length by width: 2 × 5 = 10 Multiply by the height: 10 × 7 = 70
level1.explanationEs: Multiplica el largo por el ancho: 2 × 5 = 10 Multiplica por el alto: 10 × 7 = 70

level1.stem: A box is 3 inches long, 3 inches wide, and 10 inches tall. What is the total volume of 2 of these boxes?
level1.stemEs: Una caja mide 3 pulgadas de largo, 3 de ancho y 10 de alto. ¿Cuál es el volumen total de 2 de estas cajas?
hints: Find one box's volume. Then multiply by 2.
hintsEs: Halla el volumen de una caja. Luego multiplica por 2.
level1.explanation: Find the volume of one box: 3 × 3 × 10 = 90 Multiply by 2 boxes: 90 × 2 = 180
level1.explanationEs: Halla el volumen de una caja: 3 × 3 × 10 = 90 Multiplica por 2 cajas: 90 × 2 = 180

level1.stem: A box is 4 inches long, 2 inches wide, and 6 inches tall. What is the total volume of 3 of these boxes?
level1.stemEs: Una caja mide 4 pulgadas de largo, 2 de ancho y 6 de alto. ¿Cuál es el volumen total de 3 de estas cajas?
hints: Find one box's volume. Then multiply by 3.
hintsEs: Halla el volumen de una caja. Luego multiplica por 3.
level1.explanation: Find the volume of one box: 4 × 2 × 6 = 48 Multiply by 3 boxes: 48 × 3 = 144
level1.explanationEs: Halla el volumen de una caja: 4 × 2 × 6 = 48 Multiplica por 3 cajas: 48 × 3 = 144

level1.stem: A box is 3 inches long, 2 inches wide, and 5 inches tall. What is its volume?
level1.stemEs: Una caja mide 3 pulgadas de largo, 2 de ancho y 5 de alto. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
hints: Multiply length × width × height.
hintsEs: Multiplica largo × ancho × alto.
level1.explanation: Multiply length by width: 3 × 2 = 6 Multiply by the height: 6 × 5 = 30
level1.explanationEs: Multiplica el largo por el ancho: 3 × 2 = 6 Multiplica por el alto: 6 × 5 = 30

level1.stem: A box is 9 inches long, 3 inches wide, and 12 inches tall. What is the total volume of 2 of these boxes?
level1.stemEs: Una caja mide 9 pulgadas de largo, 3 de ancho y 12 de alto. ¿Cuál es el volumen total de 2 de estas cajas?
hints: Find the volume of one box first. Then multiply by 2.
hintsEs: Primero halla el volumen de una caja. Luego multiplica por 2.
level1.explanation: Find the volume of one box: 9 × 3 × 12 = 324 Multiply by 2 boxes: 324 × 2 = 648
level1.explanationEs: Halla el volumen de una caja: 9 × 3 × 12 = 324 Multiplica por 2 cajas: 324 × 2 = 648

level2.stem: Pack A has 4 boxes of 120 cubic inches. Pack B has 2 boxes of 200 cubic inches. Leo says Pack B holds more because its boxes are bigger. How many more cubic inches does Pack A hold?
level2.stemEs: El paquete A tiene 4 cajas de 120 pulgadas cúbicas. El paquete B tiene 2 cajas de 200 pulgadas cúbicas. Leo dice que el paquete B contiene más porque sus cajas son más grandes. ¿Cuántas pulgadas cúbicas más contiene el paquete A?
hints: Bigger boxes are not enough. Find the total volume of each pack.
hintsEs: Las cajas más grandes no bastan. Halla el volumen total de cada paquete.
level2.explanation: Find the total for Pack A: 120 × 4 = 480 Find the total for Pack B: 200 × 2 = 400 Compare the totals: 480 − 400 = 80
level2.explanationEs: Halla el total del paquete A: 120 × 4 = 480 Halla el total del paquete B: 200 × 2 = 400 Compara los totales: 480 − 400 = 80

level2.stem: Box C is 2 in by 3 in by 7 in. Box D is 3 in by 3 in by 5 in. How many more cubic inches does Box D hold?
level2.stemEs: La caja C mide 2 in por 3 in por 7 in. La caja D mide 3 in por 3 in por 5 in. ¿Cuántas pulgadas cúbicas más contiene la caja D?
hints: Find both volumes. Then subtract.
hintsEs: Halla los dos volúmenes. Luego resta.
level2.explanation: Find the volume of Box C: 2 × 3 × 7 = 42 Find the volume of Box D: 3 × 3 × 5 = 45 Subtract the volumes: 45 − 42 = 3
level2.explanationEs: Halla el volumen de la caja C: 2 × 3 × 7 = 42 Halla el volumen de la caja D: 3 × 3 × 5 = 45 Resta los volúmenes: 45 − 42 = 3

level2.stem: A box is 7 inches long, 2 inches wide, and 10 inches tall. What is the total volume of 3 of these boxes?
level2.stemEs: Una caja mide 7 pulgadas de largo, 2 de ancho y 10 de alto. ¿Cuál es el volumen total de 3 de estas cajas?
hints: Find one box's volume. Then multiply by 3.
hintsEs: Halla el volumen de una caja. Luego multiplica por 3.
level2.explanation: Find the volume of one box: 7 × 2 × 10 = 140 Multiply by 3 boxes: 140 × 3 = 420
level2.explanationEs: Halla el volumen de una caja: 7 × 2 × 10 = 140 Multiplica por 3 cajas: 140 × 3 = 420

level2.stem: Pack A has 3 boxes, each 10 in by 2 in by 9 in. Pack B has 2 boxes, each 9 in by 4 in by 8 in. How many more cubic inches does Pack B hold?
level2.stemEs: El paquete A tiene 3 cajas de 10 in por 2 in por 9 in cada una. El paquete B tiene 2 cajas de 9 in por 4 in por 8 in cada una. ¿Cuántas pulgadas cúbicas más contiene el paquete B?
hints: Find one box's volume in each pack. Multiply by the number of boxes. Then subtract.
hintsEs: Halla el volumen de una caja de cada paquete. Multiplica por el número de cajas. Luego resta.
level2.explanation: Find the total for Pack A: 10 × 2 × 9 = 180; 180 × 3 = 540 Find the total for Pack B: 9 × 4 × 8 = 288; 288 × 2 = 576 Subtract the totals: 576 − 540 = 36
level2.explanationEs: Halla el total del paquete A: 10 × 2 × 9 = 180; 180 × 3 = 540 Halla el total del paquete B: 9 × 4 × 8 = 288; 288 × 2 = 576 Resta los totales: 576 − 540 = 36

level2.stem: Tank A is 20 inches long, 10 inches wide, and 12 inches tall. Tank B is 15 inches long, 12 inches wide, and 14 inches tall. How many more cubic inches does the bigger tank hold?
level2.stemEs: La pecera A mide 20 pulgadas de largo, 10 de ancho y 12 de alto. La pecera B mide 15 pulgadas de largo, 12 de ancho y 14 de alto. ¿Cuántas pulgadas cúbicas más contiene la pecera mayor?
hints: Find the volume of each tank. Then subtract the smaller from the bigger.
hintsEs: Halla el volumen de cada pecera. Luego resta la menor de la mayor.
level2.explanation: Find the volume of Tank A: 20 × 10 × 12 = 2,400 Find the volume of Tank B: 15 × 12 × 14 = 2,520 Subtract the volumes: 2,520 − 2,400 = 120
level2.explanationEs: Halla el volumen de la pecera A: 20 × 10 × 12 = 2,400 Halla el volumen de la pecera B: 15 × 12 × 14 = 2,520 Resta los volúmenes: 2,520 − 2,400 = 120

level3.stem: Zoe claims, “Two boxes always hold more than one box.” One big box is 10 in by 6 in by 10 in. Two small boxes are each 5 in by 4 in by 10 in. How many more cubic inches does the big box hold?
level3.stemEs: Zoe afirma: «Dos cajas siempre contienen más que una caja». Una caja grande mide 10 in por 6 in por 10 in. Dos cajas pequeñas miden 5 in por 4 in por 10 in cada una. ¿Cuántas pulgadas cúbicas más contiene la caja grande?
hints: Find the big box's volume. Then find the total for the two small boxes.
hintsEs: Halla el volumen de la caja grande. Luego halla el total de las dos cajas pequeñas.
level3.explanation: Find the volume of the big box: 10 × 6 × 10 = 600 Find the total for two small boxes: 5 × 4 × 10 = 200; 200 × 2 = 400 Subtract the totals: 600 − 400 = 200
level3.explanationEs: Halla el volumen de la caja grande: 10 × 6 × 10 = 600 Halla el total de las dos cajas pequeñas: 5 × 4 × 10 = 200; 200 × 2 = 400 Resta los totales: 600 − 400 = 200

level3.stem: Box G is 5 in by 2 in by 12 in. Box H is 4 in by 4 in by 8 in. How many more cubic inches does Box H hold?
level3.stemEs: La caja G mide 5 in por 2 in por 12 in. La caja H mide 4 in por 4 in por 8 in. ¿Cuántas pulgadas cúbicas más contiene la caja H?
hints: Find both volumes. Then subtract.
hintsEs: Halla los dos volúmenes. Luego resta.
level3.explanation: Find the volume of Box G: 5 × 2 × 12 = 120 Find the volume of Box H: 4 × 4 × 8 = 128 Subtract the volumes: 128 − 120 = 8
level3.explanationEs: Halla el volumen de la caja G: 5 × 2 × 12 = 120 Halla el volumen de la caja H: 4 × 4 × 8 = 128 Resta los volúmenes: 128 − 120 = 8

level3.stem: Sam claims, “A taller fish tank always holds more water.” Which pair of tanks shows that Sam is wrong?
level3.stemEs: Sam afirma: «Una pecera más alta siempre contiene más agua». ¿Qué par de peceras muestra que Sam está equivocado?
hints: Look for a pair where the taller tank holds LESS.
hintsEs: Busca un par donde la pecera más alta contenga MENOS.
level3.explanation: Find the taller tank in each pair: 20 in > 10 in Check if the taller tank holds less: 2,000 < 3,000
level3.explanationEs: Halla la pecera más alta de cada par: 20 in > 10 in Revisa si la más alta contiene menos: 2,000 < 3,000
choices: A 20 in tall tank holds 2,000 cu in. A 10 in tall tank holds 3,000 cu in.
A 20 in tall tank holds 2,000 cu in. A 15 in tall tank holds 1,500 cu in.
Two tanks are both 12 in tall. One holds 480 cu in and one holds 400 cu in.
choicesEs: Una pecera de 20 in de alto contiene 2,000 in³. Una de 10 in de alto contiene 3,000 in³.
Una pecera de 20 in de alto contiene 2,000 in³. Una de 15 in de alto contiene 1,500 in³.
Dos peceras miden 12 in de alto. Una contiene 480 in³ y la otra 400 in³.
choiceFeedback: Here the taller tank holds more. That agrees with Sam, so it is not a counterexample.
Both tanks are the same height, so they cannot test a claim about taller tanks.

level3.stem: Box P is 2 in by 3 in by 10 in. Box Q has a 5 in by 6 in bottom. What is the shortest whole-inch height that makes Box Q hold more than Box P?
level3.stemEs: La caja P mide 2 in por 3 in por 10 in. La caja Q tiene una base de 5 in por 6 in. ¿Cuál es la menor altura en pulgadas enteras que hace que la caja Q contenga más que la caja P?
hints: Find Box P's volume. Then test heights for Box Q. Equal is not more.
hintsEs: Halla el volumen de la caja P. Luego prueba alturas para la caja Q. Igual no es más.
level3.explanation: Find the volume of Box P: 2 × 3 × 10 = 60 Find the area of Box Q's bottom: 5 × 6 = 30 Test heights 2 and 3: 30 × 2 = 60; 30 × 3 = 90
level3.explanationEs: Halla el volumen de la caja P: 2 × 3 × 10 = 60 Halla el área de la base de la caja Q: 5 × 6 = 30 Prueba las alturas 2 y 3: 30 × 2 = 60; 30 × 3 = 90

level3.stem: A student claims: “Greater box volume ALWAYS means more cereal inside.” Which is the best counterexample?
choices: A large box that costs more than a jumbo box
A jumbo box with more volume that is sold half-filled with air
Two jumbo boxes that are easier to store than three large boxes
A box of a different cereal brand
level3.explanation: A counterexample must break the claim itself: a bigger box holding less cereal (more air) shows greater volume does not guarantee more cereal.
choiceFeedback: Price does not test the claim — the claim links volume to AMOUNT of cereal, not cost.
Storage convenience is a different argument entirely; it says nothing about how much cereal is inside.
Changing the brand changes the product, but does not show a bigger box holding less cereal.
hints: A counterexample must make the claim FALSE in one case.
The claim connects volume to amount of cereal.
Find the case where volume is bigger but cereal is not.
level3.stemEs: Un estudiante afirma: “Más volumen de caja SIEMPRE significa más cereal adentro.” ¿Cuál es el mejor contraejemplo?
level3.explanationEs: Un contraejemplo debe romper la afirmación misma: una caja más grande que contiene menos cereal (más aire) muestra que más volumen no garantiza más cereal.
hintsEs: Un contraejemplo debe hacer FALSA la afirmación en un caso.
La afirmación conecta el volumen con la cantidad de cereal.
Halla el caso donde el volumen es mayor pero el cereal no.

tool.caption: Three large boxes hold 240 x 3 = 720 cubic inches; two jumbo boxes hold 400 x 2 = 800. The taller bar is the evidence an equation argument would point at.
